hints: The graph has positive flight costs, but several different routes to the same city may be needed.
Store up to k shortest distances per city in a min-priority queue.
When a city is popped fewer than k times, extend its routes along outgoing edges.
analogy: Keep the first k cheapest arrivals at each city instead of only one best arrival.
example: If a destination has route costs 5,7,9, the three outputs are those costs in order.
algorithm: Use a min-heap of (distance,city) and a pop counter per city. Expand an entry only while that city's counter is below k; record distances when destination is popped.
correctness: Heap order emits route costs globally from smallest upward; retaining k pops at each vertex preserves every prefix route needed among the first k destination routes.
complexity: O(km log(km)) upper bound and O(km) queue storage.
